whatIsIt.eyebrow: Do you need a software factory?
whatIsIt.leadHtml: Is your AI development a set of silos? Do you need to bring structure to your agentic development? And have cost-awareness along the way?
whatIsIt.paragraph1Html: A software factory is a mechanised way of delivering hardened software with AI. A factory takes raw inputs and produces consistent outputs. In a software factory, your raw inputs are ideas - feature requests, bug reports, and new projects. Your outputs: merge requests, completed code, testable artifacts, and reports.
whatIsIt.paragraph2Html: A good software factory also recognizes when human input is needed, but can proceed autonomously as much as it can. It is a productivity multiplier, not a walled garden. It is a foundation for productive software development. Thus the name, Yesod (foundation).

items.body: Before we do, we listen. We make sure that we have a good fit in terms of workflow, AI maturity, scale, requirements.

How can we make a software factory that works for you? How does your team work? What processes do you want standardized? Where would you like human in the loop? How do you pay for tokens? What are your compliance requirements?
We install the software factory according to your requirements, extensively test, and provide training to make sure it works with your team. Regular check-ins ensure maximum utilization.
Is your desired output a testable iPhone app? Do you want to talk to the factory exclusively over Slack? Does this need to run air-gapped?

process.body: The most important part of a software factory is - does it work for your team? That is where MeshCrawler can help.
